speakers: Jim Rogers (co-founder of Quantum Fund, creator of Rogers International Commodities Index)
Amir and Owen (hosts, Generating Alpha podcast)
summary: Jim Rogers, Quantum Fund co-founder, on his career, travels and views. Discretionary global multi-asset long/short with commodities. Main views: China rising again, US debt and money printing are long-term problems, agriculture to recover; avoid hot tips and invest in what you know.

coverage.note: intro, childhood and discovering Wall Street; no method content
China on the rise again, first job, study what you love
first major investment and losing everything on shorts, early hedge funds
Quantum fund purpose, own approach vs others, multi-asset long/short, commodities
need to know everything incl. commodity prices; travel lessons
travel views, advice to follow passions; nothing actionable
focus passions; mentors; investment process today; Uzbekistan bullish
stop-loss answer, China rise, agriculture view, central bank concerns start
money printing and debasement, US debt, avoid hot tips

claims.speaker: Jim Rogers
claims.quote: China is the only country in world history that's been on top three or four times
claims.claim: China is the only country that has risen to the top repeatedly after collapsing, so its current rise is a recurring cycle and investors and students should know China and Chinese.
claims.conditions: He admits he does not know why it recurs
claims.testable: no - single country history, small sample

claims.speaker: Jim Rogers
claims.quote: my shorts went through the roof even though they later went bankrupt didn't do to me any good because I lost everything first
claims.claim: Being right on the thesis does not help if timing is wrong: his shorts on companies that later went bankrupt first soared in a rising market and wiped him out, so the market is harder to read than the analysis and there is more emotion than expected.
claims.indicator: short positions in a rising market
claims.conditions: Shorting into a market euphoria; investors committed to losing positions can be forced out before the thesis plays out
claims.testable: yes - short-squeeze and stop-out risk can be backtested

claims.speaker: Jim Rogers
claims.quote: people try to get washed away in other people's strategies
claims.claim: Investors fail by adopting other people's strategies they do not understand instead of sticking to the approach that has worked for them; there are many ways to make money (Roy Neuberger traded ticks, Rogers studied companies), so find what suits you.

claims.speaker: Jim Rogers
claims.quote: we invested in everything stocks bonds currencies commodities all over the world long and short
claims.claim: The Quantum approach was a global multi-asset long/short portfolio across stocks, bonds, currencies and commodities, with commodities seen as important inputs (for example copper for power plants).
claims.direction: long and short across asset classes
claims.testable: partly - multi-asset long/short construction is testable

claims.speaker: Jim Rogers
claims.quote: if you don't know the price of copper you're going to suffer somewhere
claims.claim: Everything in the world (commodity prices of copper and wheat, technology) affects investments, so a successful investor must know as much as possible about global developments.
claims.testable: partly - cross-asset linkages testable, 'know everything' is not

claims.speaker: Jim Rogers
claims.quote: I am extremely bullish on usbekistan these days for what it's worth it doesn't mean I know what I'm doing
claims.claim: He is very bullish on Uzbekistan, a country he says was once among the most successful in the world, and thinks it is an investable place that most people have not heard of.
claims.conditions: He gives a historical reason (Tamerlane) rather than data and says he may be wrong
claims.testable: no - view with weak stated reasoning

claims.speaker: Jim Rogers
claims.quote: my pathetic answer usually is I just take the pain until I realize oh I made a bad mistake and finally take the loss
claims.claim: He has no rule for cutting losses: some use stop-losses (e.g. out if it falls 12%), he holds through the pain until he sees he made a mistake.
claims.conditions: He admits he has no good answer
claims.testable: yes - stop-loss rules can be backtested

claims.speaker: Jim Rogers
claims.quote: whenever you find a dis disaster especially if it's something the world needs and it changes you'll probably be very successful
claims.claim: Agriculture has been a disaster sector for a long time and unpopular with young people (none want to be farmers), so something the world needs that is out of favour is likely to improve and reward early investors.

claims.speaker: Jim Rogers
claims.quote: there are very few countries that have become successful by debasing the currency
claims.claim: Central banks printing money to solve problems is a temporary fix that rarely succeeds long term, because few countries become successful by debasing their currency.
claims.testable: partly - debasement and growth studies exist

claims.speaker: Jim Rogers
claims.quote: the US has become the largest debtor nation in the history of the world
claims.claim: The US, a creditor nation until about 1987, now has staggering and skyrocketing debts; like Britain, which kept borrowing until it went bankrupt and needed an IMF bailout, the US could face a crisis.
claims.indicator: US external debtor position; government debt
claims.conditions: Britain analogy after being the richest country 100 years ago

claims.speaker: Jim Rogers
claims.quote: the best advice I can give you is only invest in what you yourself know a lot about
claims.claim: Ignore hot tips and copying others' trades: without knowing why you bought you cannot decide what to do when the price moves, so invest only in what you know well.
